newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES TOP BRAVES IN INTERLEAGUE MARQUEE MATCHUP.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES TOP BRAVES IN INTERLEAGUE MARQUEE MATCHUP.

text.p: Jimmy Key became the third 11-game winner in the majors and Brady Anderson, Rafael Palmeiro and Cal Ripken delivered RBI singles as the Baltimore Orioles edged the Atlanta Braves 4-3 in a meeting of the teams with the best records in each league.
Key (11-1), who beat the Braves in Game 6 of the World Series last year with the Yankees, allowed one run and five hits with three walks and six strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings.
Armando Benitez surrendered solo homers to Chipper Jones and Eduardo Perez in the eighth, but Randy Myers notched his major league-leading 21st save to seal the AL team's victory.
The Orioles broke a scoreless tie with four runs in the sixth off Braves starter Greg Maddux (7-3).

"It was a great game to play, it had such potential," Ripken enthused. "Jimmy Key and Maddux dominated as expected and kept the game close. It kind of felt like an All-Star game atmosphere, it was very exciting."

In New York, John Valentin and Troy O'Leary hit back-to-back homers in the fifth and Mo Vaughn added a two-run shot as the Boston Red Sox beat the Mets 8-4 in the first meeting between the clubs since the 1986 World Series.
The Mets hit four solo homers -- two by Carl Everett.

Jeff Suppan (1-0) allowing two runs and eight hits in five innings for the win. Mets starter Rick Reed (4-4) retired the first 13 batters he faced but faltered in the fifth to take the loss after giving up five runs on six hits in six innings.
"Suppan pitched great," said Red Sox manager Jimy Williams. "He did not get caught up in all the interleague hype. We played by their rules ... and fortunatley we won."
In Chicago, Jose Valentin homered and drove in three runs and Jeff D'Amico pitched eight strong innings to lead the Milwaukee Brewers to a 4-2 win over the Cubs.
Valentin hit a two-run homer in the second and added an RBI double in the fourth to stake the Brewers to a 3-0 lead.
D'Amico (3-3) allowed two runs and five hits to earn the win. Chicago's Terry Mulholland (5-6) lasted 6 2/3 innings and yielded four runs and eight hits for the loss.
In Cincinnati, Wilson Alvarez allowed one run in 7 2/3 innings and Albert Belle hit a two-run homer to lead the Chicago White Sox to a 3-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
It was the first meeting between the teams since the infamous 1919 World Series when eight members of the White Sox were found guilty of conspiring to throw the series.
Cincinnati's Pete Schourek (5-5) allowed just three hits but two of them were home runs by Belle and Ray Durham.
At Florida, Charles Johnson walked with the bases loaded to force in the winning run in the bottom of the 12th inning and give the Marlins a 2-1 victory over the New York Yankees.
Jim Mecir (0-4) started the 12th for New York and loaded the bases thanks to some shaky defensive play. Johnson then patiently walked on a 3-2 pitch to force in the winning run.
Dennis Cook (1-0) picked up the win by getting out of a bases loaded jam in the top of the 12th.

In Philadelphia, Gregg Jefferies delivered a two-out, two-run single in the seventh inning to lead the Phillies to a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays in the first meeting between the teams since the 1993 World Series.

Jefferies stroked a bases-loaded single through the left side of the infield, scoring Mickey Morandini and Darren Daulton for a 3-2 lead. The Phils added an insurance run in the eighth on a wild pitch.
Wayne Gomes (1-0) got the win for one inning of relief in his major-league debut. Paul Spoljaric (0-3) took the loss.
In Houston, Chuck Knoblauch went 4-for-4 with three RBI and Brad Radke pitched eight strong innings as the Minnesota Twins routed the Astros 8-1.
Knoblauch delivered a two-out, two-run triple in the fourth that gave Minnesota a three-run lead. He ended up with with two singles and a double, in addition to the triple.
Radke (6-5) allowed one run and six hits with one walk and five strikeouts. Donne Wall (2-3) took the loss.

In Montreal, Carlos Perez pitched 7 1/3 strong innings and Henry Rodriguez and Darrin Fletcher each had two hits and two RBI to lead the Expos to a 4-3 win over the Detroit Tigers, extending their winning streak to seven.
Perez ran his scoreless innings streak to 22 2/3 before Brian Hunter doubled home pitcher Omar Olivares with two out in the top of the fifth.
With American League pitchers forced to hit in interleague games in NL parks, Olivares became the first AL pitcher to hit a triple since Milwaukee's Ed Rodriguez in 1973.

In Pittsburgh, Tony Womack hit a solo homer with two out in the sixth inning after former Royal Joe Randa tied the game with a home run in the fifth as the Pirates rallied past the Kansas City Royals, 5-3.

Womack drove a 0-1 offering from reliever Mike Williams (0-2) over the right-field wall to break a 3-3 tie. The Pirates added an insurance run in the seventh when Jason Kendall came home on Randa's sacrifice fly.
